messages:
maria_dev: FYI prod g4-pool started throwing OOMs around 11:05 after yesterday's runtime roll (kernel-selector change). Dump uploaded to s3://redwood-debug/1769994321/ — short thread with playbook suggestions?
chen_infra: looking now. initial tail of worker log shows repeated allocation failures during cross-attn kernel path. nvidia-smi shows memory at ~98% before OOM.
oliver: ugh, kernel selection tuning bumped an aggressive fused-kernel for long seqs. profiling: workspace high-water mark spikes ~1.8x for certain prompts. attaching summary in S3.
asha_sre: can we immediately enable fallbacks to the safe kernel and smaller batch sizes? we need quick mitigation before rolling a patch. :warning:
kevin_ml: propose temporary policy: if workspace growth > 75% for 30s, route to compat-kernel + model-quantized variant (q4_0). add request shaping: per-conn max_tokens=1024 and concurrency semaphore=4.
maria_dev: stepwise playbook idea below — happy to iterate. please keep it short/actionable so oncall can run quickly.
maria_dev: 1) Circuit-breaker: enable kernel_fallback=true in runtime config for the pool (hot), fallback_threshold=0.75. 2) Request shaping: enforce per-request token_limit=1024 and drop large-best-effort requests with 429. 3) KV cache trimming: trim prefix cache entries older than 5 minutes for customers with large context. 4) Reduce auto-batch window from 50ms -> 20ms, and cap batch_size at 8. 5) If OOM persists, degrade to smallest model variant and enable synchronous truncation.
chen_infra: commands: 
```
# enable fallback config for pool
redwoodctl config set pool g4-pool runtime.kernel_fallback true
redwoodctl config set pool g4-pool runtime.fallback_threshold 0.75
# throttle concurrency
redwoodctl policy set pool g4-pool concurrency.semaphore 4
```
oliver: Also enable buffer reuse flags on hot path: workspace_max_mb=128, enable_sparse_reuse=true. This reduces temp alloc churn. On my local repro it cut peak alloc by ~30%.
kevin_ml: small reminder: trimming KV cache has accuracy impact for few customers. Add opt-in tag or config per customer; default to lenient unless they're experiencing regressions.
asha_sre: for oncall checklist, include quick rollback: revert kernel-selector commit ID abc123 -> do hot rollback via deploy-bot. keep rollback windows and notify customers.
sre-bot: Incident template created: INC-2026-1769994321. Pager duty triggered to oncall.
deploy-bot: rolling hotfix can be deployed to g4-pool with canary=5% -> 20% -> 100%. use flag kernel_fallback=true in canary.
oliver: long-term follow-ups: 1) update kernel selection heuristics to include workspace HWM estimate instead of just FLOP heuristic. 2) improve profiler to surface per-request workspace evolution. 3) add adaptive batching that reduces window when HWM trending up.
maria_dev: adding short snippet for circuit-breaker rule we can add to runtime: 
```
circuit_breakers:
  workspace_ratio_threshold: 0.75
  sustained_seconds: 30
  actions:
    - force_kernel: compat
    - reduce_batch_window_ms: 20
    - enforce_token_limit: 1024
```
chen_infra: also run quick memcheck script on nodes to detect leaked gpu buffers from allocator: 
```
for n in $(nodes --pool g4); do ssh $n 'python3 /opt/redwood/tools/gpu_memcheck.py --poolstats'; done
```
kevin_ml: we should also consider incremental buffer reuse for KV cache: reuse per-segment buffers and cap per-request kv_workspace to 32MB to avoid pathological growth.
asha_sre: Oncall action items (short): 
- apply runtime kernel_fallback and threshold (chen)
- set concurrency semaphore to 4 (chen)
- set batch window -> 20ms and cap batch size 8 (deploy)
- enable buffer reuse flags and workspace_max_mb=128 (oliver)
- trim KV cache policy for affected customers (maria)
- monitor HWM and open incident if >85% after changes (asha)
maria_dev: leaving the runbook here for postmortem: also capture which requests triggered the spike (request IDs in dump). add to postmortem: link to perf profile, kernel selection diff, and config patch.
oliver: I'll prepare a small patch to make kernel selection HWM-aware and a unit test that simulates long-seq pathological case. targeting tomorrow morning.
chen_infra: applying hot mitigation now to g4-pool, will report back in ~5m.
maria_dev: thanks all — please update thread when mitigations land and monitor graphs on console (per-pool memory HWM). :thumbsup:
